first_installment_sketch: The double-bill beat: a dispatched call times out and nobody knows whether the effect happened. The wrong answers: retry blindly and double-charge the customer, or give up silently and lose the work. The right answer: UNKNOWN goes to HOLD, then reconcile, never blind redispatch. The installment labels honestly that HOLD and recovery behavior is specified but not yet reached behavior.
hook: We do not know is a state. Treating it as failure is a bug.
thesis: FAILURE IS A STATE is a recurring franchise: UNKNOWN effects, HOLD, reconcile, never blind retry. Each installment takes one failure mode where systems silently drop, double-execute, or mislabel what happened, shows the typed semantics Orca assigns it, and names the reconcile path. Failure must have typed, deterministic semantics; an empty answer never hides an infrastructure failure.
title: FAILURE IS A STATE
